Mass Effect series ended with this game. That other game claiming to be Mass Effect should have not been named Mass Effect.

I havent touched the single player because honestly I do not care about it in the slightest. If you want a review for the singleplayer, Look elsewhere. BUT, I can reccomend this game solely for the multiplayer alone, if a co-op, 3rd-person class shooter survival is something you're interested in. 

A few things to note going into this right off the bat though that very well might turn people off, and rightly so: 

1) Origin's overlay cuases FPS issues in the game that are yet to be fixed as of the time of this revview. However, in my experience, it hasn't once dipped to the point of unplayability, or even to the point where I suffered an unfair death, and its usually stable on my rig. But if you're the sort of person who cant tolerate that, hold off.

2) the free multiplayer DLC from when the game was originally on console is now FORCIBLY BUNDLED with all the single player DLC, whin means you cant get most of the classes, weapons and maps without it, nor can you play with people that own the DLC. It pissed me off a bit, but as of writing, all the DLC and the game was on sale for 40 bucks, so honestly it's not the worst, but I'd prefer not to give EA money for stuff that was once free (but my feeling of nostalgia overrides my desire to hold onto 20 bucks)

3) the game still functions off loot boxes. Granted, they are not nearly as bad as modern loot boxes, but they're there. 

With that out of the way, in my experience, the multiplayer is still a blast to play, even with random people, but it's most fun with friends. If it interests you, pick it up while its cheap. If not, I STRONGLY suggest waiting until Bioware fixes the issues people are experiencing, because my experience and lack of technical issues doesn't mean you won't have them.

First off, ignore my review time, I owned a copy of ME3 on Origin for years and have played through the game multiple times. I bought it on Steam simply to have everything in one place. 

ME3 is the culmination to the Mass Effect Trilogy (outside of Andromeda - Which does it's own thing) and your decisions from ME1 and ME2 carry over to Mass Effect 3, as you'd probably expect. Mass Effect 3's gameplay can be summarized as an refinement of 2's. You have the over-the-shoulder gunplay in third person, combined with class skills, with the ability to tailor the abilities of your crew and such. It's one of the last good Bioware Games in that it's heavily story based and offers you a tremendous deal of choices (except for the ending, I'll touch on that later). 

The characters in both ME2 and Mass Effect 3 are some of my favorites in video games period, especially Garrus and Tali'Zorah (two of your crew members / party members). Each Companion has story quests that expand on their backstories (although for more info you really should play Mass Effect 1 and 2, seriously), and of course you can romance many of them, in fact the famous meme "We'll Bang OK" kinda comes from this game (it's not a literal line though), and for good reason. 

The Story of ME3 is pretty good, not as good as 2 (Seriously, go play it) but it ends the whole trilogy and concludes the story of the Reapers, a race of sentient cyborgs bent on destroying all life and assimilating it (Like Borg from Star Trek) and finally lets you destroy them. For context, one scout reaper in Mass Effect 1 destroyed a fleet of Alliance Ships, in 2, the Reapers nearly invaded before being delayed by Shepard, and in 3, they finally get here after being hyped up for 2 games. Understandably, they basically start ROFL-Stomping the Galaxy by zerg rushing everything, and it's up to Shepard (You) to help the Alliance, get allies against the Reapers, and take the Galaxy back. 

There is one point that the story doesn't do well on, the ending. Initially Bioware even released a free DLC to fix the ending after fan backlash (unfortunately the Steam version is in the DLC Bundle which is NOT free). It still doesn't do the series justice IMO, but you may think otherwise. It basically boils down to three endings you choose at the end which all basically give blanket stories of how the universe does afterwards, without really giving you glimpses of how your crew is afterwards, which really sucks as you spent basically 3 whole games building up your relationship with them. 

The game also has Multiplayer which unfortunately is tied in to the singleplayer and required to unlock certain story paths. The galactic readiness stat which goes up as you win matches is used to determine if some big singleplayer decisions can be made, like saving two species instead of choosing 1 to live and 1 to die (not spoiling who they are). Multiplayer itself is kinda fun actually, it's Horde mode with Co-Op, and classes are unique to the multiplayer (advanced ones anyways), so you can have a stealthy Turian or a Human N7 Operative with (Power Armor, Cybernetic Ninja Gear, or Special Biotics) among others. Also it's fairly easy to earn credits to get packs to unlock stuff, just play medium and hard difficulty waves, don't bother spending money on MTX when it's easily earnable through gameplay. Besides the game is a few years old and can use more multiplayer people. 

Overall I'd say that if you're  a fan of RPGs and Sci-Fi, you owe it to yourself to pick Mass Effect 3 up, although I'd HEAVILY recommend playing Mass Effect 2 BEFORE you play Mass Effect 3. You can skip Mass Effect 1 provided you have the Genesis DLC for 2, it lets you choose the story options from 1 to make a world-state for ME2, and ME3 lets you import your story stuff from ME2. After you're done with ME3 you can play Andromeda too I guess, but it's story is nowhere near as good as the OG Trilogy (1-3).
